segments.text: Hello.
Two weeks.
Fourteen days ago you were getting through a first day, one wave at a time.
I'd like you to take a second with that, because it's easy to rush past.
The first stretch, the steepest one, is behind you.
The changes at two weeks are rarely dramatic.
They're quiet, and you have to look for them.
You're not planning your day around charging, refilling or buying.
The money stays with you.
And some people find their throat or breathing feels easier over time.
And there are changes that have nothing to do with your body.
You've sat through cravings and watched them pass.
You've had hard days and not reached for the old answer.
You know something about yourself now that you didn't know a month ago.
Let's look for one change together.
Take a breath, in a way that feels comfortable for you.
Think back to an ordinary moment from the last few days.
A morning.
A meal.
A drive.
Was the gap in it?
That restless pull, every hour or two?
Or was it simply a morning?
Now think of one thing that's easier than it was two weeks ago.
Anything at all.
Hold on to that one.
It's yours, and you earned it.
In a moment, your numbers will be on your screen.
Your days, the cravings you've ridden out, and the money you've kept.
And your check-in, beside the one from your first morning.
Then, the same as last week, choose something small for yourself, and pay for it out of what you've kept.
It isn't a prize for being good.
It's what that money is for now.
Some days will still be harder than others.
A hard day doesn't undo the good ones.
Two weeks.
Keep going.
It's working.
I'll see you in a couple of days.
